table_description: UDTF that returns one row per active job currently on the system. Snapshot view — call it repeatedly for time-series. The single most useful function for runtime diagnosis. Cardinality is roughly the number of active jobs (typically 100s – 1000s).

table_columns.name: JOB_NAME
table_columns.description: Fully qualified job name in 'number/user/name' format (e.g. '123456/QUSER/QPADEV0001'). Use this verbatim as the WHERE filter for follow-up calls like JOBLOG_INFO.

table_columns.name: SUBSYSTEM
table_columns.description: Subsystem the job is running under (e.g. 'QINTER', 'QBATCH', 'QHTTPSVR'). Common filter for narrowing to a workload class.

table_columns.name: JOB_TYPE
table_columns.description: 'INT' = interactive, 'BCH' = batch, 'BCI' = batch immediate, 'SBS' = subsystem monitor, 'SYS' = system job, 'AUT' = autostart, 'WTR' = writer.

table_columns.name: CPU_PERCENTAGE
table_columns.description: Job's share of total CPU since its activation, not last-second instantaneous. For instantaneous CPU pressure, look at QSYS2.SYSTEM_STATUS_INFO.

table_columns.name: ELAPSED_CPU_PERCENTAGE
table_columns.description: CPU percentage during the elapsed interval — only populated if you called RESET_STATISTICS first. Otherwise NULL.

table_columns.name: TEMPORARY_STORAGE
table_columns.description: Temporary storage allocated to the job in megabytes. Top offenders here often indicate a runaway query.

table_columns.name: RUN_PRIORITY
table_columns.description: Scheduling priority 1-99. Lower = higher priority. Typical interactive jobs sit at 20; QBATCH at 50.

data_quality_notes: ACTIVE_JOB_INFO is a UDTF — call it as TABLE(QSYS2.ACTIVE_JOB_INFO()) in a FROM clause.
CPU_PERCENTAGE is since-job-start; for last-N-second pressure pair with QSYS2.SYSTEM_STATUS_INFO.
Reasonable filters first: SUBSYSTEM, JOB_TYPE, RUN_PRIORITY. Avoid full scans without filters.
